name: scroll-and-swap

frames.best_why: Frame 3 shows the densest stack of names with two rows caught swapping over each other.

tagline: Names roll upward and each line swaps to a copy of itself as it scrolls.
summary: A tall column of bold text scrolls smoothly; as any line crosses the middle band it slides away and an identical copy slides in behind it, so the list appears to roll over itself.
appearance: A bright blue panel filled edge to edge with white, bold, uppercase names stacked tightly down the centre. Each line is centred and large; a small 'SCROLL SLOWLY' note sits in the top corner.
behaviour: Scrolling glides the whole column upward. When a line enters the swap band it lifts away while a duplicate rises from below into its place, so briefly two copies overlap before one settles.
demo_content: A long list of invented full names from Alexandra Rodriguez to Zachary Brown, under the note 'SCROLL SLOWLY'.
search_phrases: text that rolls over as you scroll
text lines changing one at a time
bold names under a scroll prompt
use_when: A credits, member or name list should feel alive while the user scrolls through it, with each row renewing itself.
avoid_when: Every line exists twice in the DOM, so very long lists cost more, and it needs a scroll container wired by ref.
customise: Each line takes its text as children and accepts the tag, scroll offset pair, spring settings and container ref; the type, colour and column width are set by the parent.
weight_why: Over a hundred text elements each track scroll progress, though only a screenful shows.

a11y.note: Reduced-motion is ignored, and the scroll container is not focusable, so keyboard users cannot scroll it without a pointer.

props.name: springConfig
props.type: { stiffness?: number; damping?: number; mass?: number }

polish_why: Bold type on saturated blue is striking and the swap reads clearly; the demo is only a name list.
title: Scroll and Swap Text
